evidence.observation: parseArgs accepts --input, --dry-run and optional --source-commit without requiring --bucket/--endpoint: lines 68-69 only demand bucket and endpoint when dryRun is false. This is what lets the offline fixture be validated with no storage credentials and no network endpoint.

main() resolves the input dir, runs the local validateBundle check, writes publication.json into the fixture dir (line 282), and at line 285 takes the dry-run early return ('no objects uploaded') before line 290 creates any temp dir or calls downloadIndex/uploadJson. The only network-touching branch is therefore never entered.

aws() is the sole child-process path that would reach the network (spawnSync('aws', ...) with AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED to avoid metadata lookups). It is only reachable from the publish branch after the dry-run return, so the offline fixture check never spawns it.

downloadIndex() reads s3://$bucket/index.json via --endpoint-url, i.e. the remote pull that a fixture lacking network data cannot satisfy. It is called only after the dry-run return in main(), confirming the chosen check bypasses it.

The package's scripts contract separates networked generation from offline use: generate-models (line 56) drives generate-models.ts, which fetches https://models.dev/api.json and provider /models endpoints; build:offline (line 61) deliberately omits it and instead runs check:model-data (line 59, validates committed src/providers/data) plus a tygo build; generate-model-catalog (line 58) emits the JSON bundle under ../../.artifacts/model-catalog that the root check:model-catalog script validates.

claims.claim: The offline fixture check is network-safe by construction: the publisher validates a purely local JSON bundle and, under --dry-run, returns ('no objects uploaded') before creating temp dirs or invoking the aws S3 download/upload path, so no network data is required or fetched.

Running the fixture with --dry-run and an explicit --source-commit leaves parseArgs satisfied without --bucket/--endpoint and skips gitSourceCommit(), so the validation spawns neither the aws CLI nor git; the only network-capable functions (aws, downloadIndex, uploadJson) stay unreachable.

packages/ai/package.json defines an explicit offline model-data path: build:offline runs check:model-data against committed data instead of generate-models, whose generate-models.ts fetches models.dev; generate-model-catalog produces the .artifacts/model-catalog JSON that the root publisher consumes, matching the fixture layout.

The repository itself treats this path as the narrowest offline check: the root check:model-catalog script runs scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs --input .artifacts/model-catalog --dry-run, and the focused node:test suite scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.mjs builds the same JSON-only fixture and asserts the normalized publication counts; both were exercised here without network access.

conclusion: Operated the offline model-catalog fixture successfully. The narrowest valid local check is `node --test scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.mjs`, the repository's focused node:test suite that constructs a JSON-only catalog fixture and invokes scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs --dry-run; it passed (1/1). In addition, a workspace-local fixture (.prale-eval/fixture/model-catalog, 500 anthropic + 5 openai + 1 openrouter chat models, 1 image, 1 classifier) was validated with `node scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs --input .prale-eval/fixture/model-catalog --source-commit t21-offline-fixture --dry-run`, producing a normalized publication record with revision sha256-8fb10cb8e46d1c858d0faa7c2499d0ea47085fa2826f6913659aace5206dc0ff, 3 providers, 506 chat, 1 image, 1 classifier and 508 total models. Both checks are offline-safe because the dry-run branch returns before any aws S3 download/upload or git invocation, and because an explicit --source-commit removes the only other subprocess call. No tracked files, locks, git configuration, or task metadata were modified (git status shows only the new untracked .prale-eval/ directory).

validation.notes: Narrowest valid local check: the repo's own focused node:test for the model-catalog publisher. Observed 'pass 1 / fail 0' (exit 0). It needs no network, no node_modules and no aws CLI: the test builds a temp JSON-only fixture and the publisher's --dry-run path returns at scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs:285-288 (before mkdtempSync/downloadIndex/uploadJson at 290+); the sole network-capable symbol, aws() at :184-198, is never spawned. TMPDIR was pointed inside the workspace so the test's temp writes stay local. Secondary operate run: `node .prale-eval/offline-model-catalog-demo.mjs` also exited 0 and emitted the normalized publication.json summarized in the conclusion and in .prale-eval/operate-deliverable.md. Limitation: node_modules is absent, so the vitest/typescript workspace suites and tsgo typecheck (build:offline) could not be run; they were not needed for this offline check.
